question:
Sentence Correction
Instruction: Questions 11-14 consist of grammatically incorrect sentences. Choose the letter that contains the correct option.

1) _______
options: A One of all-time greatest player have recently retired from football.
B One of all-time greatest players have recently retired from football.
C One of all-time greatest players has recently retired from football.
D One of all-time greatest player has recently retired from football.
explanation:
The correct sentence uses 'players' (plural) after 'one of' and 'has' because the subject 'one' is singular.

- Other options either mismatch singular/plural forms or verbs.

options: A If you'll not feel well, you'd better go to clinic.
B If you're not feeling well, you'd better go to clinic.
C If you'll not feel well, you better go to clinic.
D If you're not feeling well, you would better go to clinic.
explanation:
The correct conditional structure is 'If you're not feeling well' followed by 'you'd better' to give advice.

 Other options use incorrect verb forms or expressions.

options: A There school takes only twenty minutes on foot.
B Their school takes only twenty minutes on foot.
C Their school takes only twenty minutes on foot.
D They're school takes only twenty minutes on foot.
explanation:
'Their' is the correct possessive pronoun to indicate ownership of the school.

 Other options incorrectly use 'There' (location) or 'They're' (they are).

options: A I wanted to first take shower and then eat snack.
B I wanted to first take shower and then eat snack.
C I wanted to first take shower and then ate snack.
D I wanted to first take shower and then eating snack.
explanation:
The correct sequence maintains parallel structure: 'take shower' and 'eat snack.'

 Other options break parallelism or use incorrect verb forms ('ate,' 'eating').
